title: Angular momentum and its conservation; Simple harmonic motion: definition and graphs; Mass–spring and pendulum
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Physics C: Mechanics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: O01-1#t4 term and clue written for the game; O01-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; R06-ap2#t4 term and clue written for the game; R06-ap2#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: O01-1#N.11, O02-1#N.4b, R06-ap2#N.6, R06-ap2#N.9.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Amplitude
items.clue: Maximum displacement of an oscillating object.

items.label: Restoring force
items.clue: Always points back to equilibrium, opposite to the displacement.

items.label: Mechanical energy
items.clue: Total K + U of a satellite and planet, constant when only gravity acts.

items.label: Circular orbit
items.clue: Satellite path with r and v both fixed, so K, U, E and L are all constant.

questions.stem: A pendulum bob swings to and fro in a small arc. At the lowest point of its swing, what are its acceleration along its path and its speed?

options.text: Acceleration along the path greatest; speed zero.
Acceleration along the path zero; speed greatest.
Acceleration along the path zero; speed also zero.
Acceleration along the path greatest; speed greatest.

questions.explanation: The lowest point is equilibrium: the restoring force along the path is zero there. The bob sped up all the way down and starts to slow on the way up, so its speed is greatest here.

questions.stem: A block attached to an ideal spring oscillates on a horizontal surface with negligible friction, with period T. The block is replaced by a block with 4 times the mass, and the new block is set oscillating with 3 times the original amplitude. The new period is how many times T?

A lump of clay moving horizontally in a straight line strikes and sticks to the outer edge of a door that is initially at rest. The door can rotate about vertical hinges with negligible friction. The collision decreases the kinetic energy of the clay–door system. Which statement about the angular momentum of the clay–door system about the hinge axis is correct?

options.text: It decreases, since the system's kinetic energy decreases.
It is the same just after the collision as it was just before.
It increases from zero, as the clay moved in a straight line.
It changes, because the hinges exert a force on the door.

questions.stem: Car 1, of mass m, drives at constant speed v along a straight road that passes a lamp post at a perpendicular distance d. Car 2, of mass 2m, drives at constant speed v/2 along a straight road that passes the same post at a perpendicular distance 3d. What is the ratio L₂/L₁ of the magnitudes of the cars' angular momenta about the post?
questions.explanation: L = mv r⊥. Car 1: mvd. Car 2: 2m × (v/2) × 3d = 3mvd. Ratio 3, the same at every point of each road.
